A bladder/urethral mass strongly suspicious for invasive urothelial carcinoma may enter screening; cystoscopy confirms diagnosis before treatment. All arms include vinblastine, deracoxib and cPD-L1 immunotherapy. Creatinine must be at most 2.0 mg/dl; previous chemotherapy/radiation are excluded. NSAIDs require a 5–14-day washout; supplements require two weeks off, and current Librela/Cytopoint are not allowed.

Radiation followed by intratumoral JEN-101 and mandatory amputation at Illinois four weeks later. Cytology/histology with alkaline phosphatase support, staging without metastasis and adequate organ function for sedation are required; the team must review all previous immune-modifying drugs.

Osteosarcoma from any primary site with lung nodules at least 5 mm on CT. The study team must confirm radiation washout of at least one week and chemotherapy/immunotherapy washout of at least three weeks, controlled primary-tumor pain if not amputated, general health and expected survival of at least nine weeks. Pleural effusion, hypoxia or respiratory distress exclude enrollment; concurrent immunosuppressive drugs are prohibited.
